statement.text: Call prime $p_n$ good if $p_n^2 > p_{n-i}p_{n+i}$ for all $i$, $1 \le i \le n-1$. Is it true that the set of $n$ for which $p_n$ is good has density 0? Are there infinitely many $n$ with $p_n p_{n+1} > p_{n-i} p_{n+1+i}$ for all $i$, $1 \le i \le n-1$?

title: Pomerance's Questions on Good Primes
